Aerodynamic Equations & Betz Limit

$$P_{\text{wind}} = \frac{1}{2} \rho A v^3$$

Theoretical wind power passing through swept area $A = \pi R^2$. Air density standard $\rho = 1.225\text{ kg/m}^3$. Notice cubic sensitivity to wind speed: doubling wind speed produces $8\times$ more kinetic energy!

$$P_{\text{mech}} = \frac{1}{2} \rho A v^3 C_p(\lambda, \beta)$$

The aerodynamic power coefficient $C_p$ represents conversion efficiency. According to the Betz Limit Theorem (1919), no wind turbine can capture more than 16/27 (59.3%) of the kinetic wind stream without stopping the air completely.

Tip Speed Ratio (λ) & Pitch Dynamics

$$\lambda = \frac{\omega R}{v_{\text{wind}}} = \frac{2\pi \cdot \text{RPM} \cdot R}{60 \cdot v_{\text{wind}}}$$

For modern 3-blade HAWT turbines, the optimal aerodynamic performance peak occurs at $\lambda \approx 8.0 - 8.2$ with blade pitch angle $\beta \approx 0^\circ$, delivering real-world $C_p \approx 0.485$ (over 81% of theoretical Betz maximum!).

$$\text{Thrust Force: } T = \frac{1}{2} \rho A v^2 C_t$$

Horizontal aerodynamic thrust load on the tower top reaches over 400 kN during maximum power production, absorbed through tower flexing and heavy reinforced foundation.
